title: Progressive JSON Relaxation Harness with Syntactic Telemetry and Recovery Policies
creator: Ava Kim
description: Introduce a focused test harness that validates a progressive 'relaxation' strategy for JSON mode enforcement on streaming responses. The harness will simulate partial emits, deliberate token corruption, and interleaved tool calls to verify that the runtime can (a) detect syntactic violations, (b) apply a deterministic relaxation policy (from strict parser -> tolerant repair -> graceful fallback), and (c) emit structured telemetry for downstream evaluation and rollouts.
background: We've observed two failure classes in production: 1) transient partial-stream parses where a strictly enforced JSON gate prematurely fails on recoverable fragments, and 2) malformed trailing tokens caused by interleaved tool outputs or model hallucination. Prior work focused on strict gate semantics and decoder circuit breakers; this ticket experiments with a staged relaxation strategy and richer telemetry to enable safe rollouts without user-visible regressions.
goals: Create deterministic scenarios for partial streaming and token corruption across seq lengths (16, 128, 1024)
Implement a 3-stage relaxation policy: strict -> syntactic-repair heuristics -> structured fallback (keyed placeholder + human-readable diagnostics)
Surface telemetry events for parse state transitions, repair actions taken, and final output verdicts
Provide a CI-ready harness that runs against multiple model variants and quantization profiles
Define success metrics for rollout canary: <0.5% increase in malformed final outputs, >90% successful auto-repair rate for targeted classes
acceptance_criteria: Harness reproducibly triggers 12 canonical failure patterns and records unified telemetry schema
Repair heuristics reduce parser-fail terminal states by at least 60% on synthetic corpus
No regression in latency P95 beyond 10ms for streaming path under canary load
Runbook and fallback behavior documented with sample dashboards and alert thresholds
PR with harness and telemetry pipeline merged and behind a feature flag
test_plan: Unit tests for syntactic-repair functions with edgecase corpus (unclosed arrays, missing commas, stray brackets)
Integration tests: simulated streaming sessions with injected tool-call tokens and mid-stream truncation
Fuzzing campaign: random token-level mutations across 100k generated JSON examples
Cross-model matrix: run harness on at least 3 representative family models and 2 quantization configs
Canary: deploy feature-flagged runtime to 1% of traffic and monitor telemetry for 72 hours
scenarios: Prefix-correct, suffix-truncated: model emits valid JSON then stream cuts off mid-value
Interleaved TOOL token: tool output appears inside object value causing stray text
Trailing comma / missing comma between objects due to temperature sampling
Replacement tokens: model outputs "<UNK>" tokens within numeric fields
Repeated delimiter bursts: tokenizer splits braces across multiple chunks
telemetry_spec: event.repair_type: insertion | deletion | comma_fix | escape_fix | truncation_pad
implementation_notes: Reuse existing parser harness utilities from ENG-271448 and ENG-214578 where appropriate (adapt to progressive policy)
Keep repair heuristics deterministic and bounded (max 8 token edits), log repair stacktrace for audits
Expose a feature flag to control relaxation aggressiveness and telemetry sampling rate
Ensure repair code runs off the hot path: attempt best-effort repair in a small synchronous loop, otherwise fallback to asynchronous worker to avoid latency SLO violations
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: aggressive repairs could mask model quality regressions -> Mitigation: attach sample diff payloads to telemetry and require manual review when auto-repair rate exceeds threshold
Risk: increased CPU on streaming path -> Mitigation: cap repair attempts and fall back to placeholder early; measure P95 under load
Risk: ambiguity between tool output and model text -> Mitigation: tighten token tagging at tool-call boundary and add heuristics that prefer preserving tool delimited segments
